header.title: AI, Optimization and Advanced Computing
header.lead: This course family exposes students to computational intelligence, formal reasoning, optimization, parallelism, and advanced computing topics that extend their ability to model complex problems.

data.text: This family brings together artificial intelligence, expert systems, formal logic, logic programming, operations research, parallel information processing, compilation, embedded systems, and related advanced topics. The courses vary in technical emphasis, but they share a concern for modeling, reasoning, search, optimization, and system-level abstraction.

data.text: The course often starts from modeling: what is the problem, what are the variables, what is known, what is uncertain, what must be optimized, and what form of reasoning is appropriate? From there, students move to algorithms, tools, examples, and sometimes small implementations.

items: [b]Reasoning-centered activities[/b]: students formalize problems before trying to compute answers.
[b]Model comparison[/b]: different representations are compared for clarity, tractability, and usefulness.
[b]Applied exercises[/b]: examples connect abstract tools with decision, automation, or system-design problems.
